body.en: Limits, sequences, series, and polynomial behaviour give students the conceptual scaffolding for calculus — and appear on the hardest ACT questions.

Informal limit: \(\lim_{x \to a}f(x) = L\) means \(f(x)\) approaches \(L\) as \(x\) approaches \(a\). Conic sections — standard forms: circle \((x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\); ellipse \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\); hyperbola \(\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\); parabola \(y=ax^2+bx+c\).

label.en: Worked example — Identify and graph a conic

body.en:
Identify the conic: \(4x^2 + 9y^2 = 36\).

Divide by 36: \(\dfrac{x^2}{9}+\dfrac{y^2}{4}=1\). This is an ellipse with \(a=3\) along \(x\)-axis and \(b=2\) along \(y\)-axis, centre \((0,0)\).

caption.en: Standard ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{9} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$ centered at $(0,0)$. The major horizontal axis has length $2a = 6$ (vertices $(\pm 3, 0)$) and the minor vertical axis has length $2b = 4$ (co-vertices $(0, \pm 2)$).

label.en: ▲ ACT Math 2 Traps & Pitfalls — Limits, Conics & Binomial Expansion

body.en:
• Indeterminate Form \(0/0\) vs. Undefined: When direct substitution into \(\lim_{x \to a} \dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\) yields \(0/0\), the limit is indeterminate — factor and cancel the common factor \((x - a)\) before re-evaluating. Do NOT write 'undefined' or 'does not exist'!
  • Focal Distance in Ellipses vs. Hyperbolas: For an ellipse, the focal distance satisfies \(c^2 = a^2 - b^2\) (where \(a > b\)). For a hyperbola, the focal distance satisfies \(c^2 = a^2 + b^2\). Confusing these two relation signs is one of the most common mistakes on ACT Math 2.
  • The \(k\)-th Term Index in Binomial Expansion: In the expansion of \((a+b)^n\), the general term is \(T_{k+1} = \binom{n}{k} a^{n-k} b^k\). The 4th term corresponds to index \(k = 3\), not \(k = 4\)! Watch negative signs when expanding expressions like \((2x - 3)^n\).
  • Infinite Series Ratio Magnitude: For \(\sum a_1 r^{n-1}\), if \(|r| \ge 1\), the series does not converge, so applying \(S = \dfrac{a_1}{1-r}\) produces a false number.

question.en: Find the 4th term in the binomial expansion of \((2x - 3)^6\).

solution.en: Using the binomial theorem general term formula \(T_{k+1} = \binom{n}{k} a^{n-k} b^k\) with \(n = 6\), \(a = 2x\), \(b = -3\), and \(k = 3\) (for the 4th term): \[ T_4 = \binom{6}{3} (2x)^{6-3} (-3)^3. \] Compute the binomial coefficient: \(\binom{6}{3} = \dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 4}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 20\). \[ T_4 = 20 \cdot (2x)^3 \cdot (-27) = 20 \cdot (8x^3) \cdot (-27) = -4320x^3. \]
